explanation: Faithfully states the stronger Kovač–Tao result: some strictly increasing positive sequence has Σ 1/(a_n + t) converging to a rational for every rational t ≠ -a_n. HasSum to a rational q is the correct encoding. Formal proof linked.

erdosproblems.com/266: Kovač and Tao proved there is a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers a_n such that Σ 1/(a_n + t) converges to a rational for every t ∈ ℚ with t ≠ −a_n for all n. The Lean statement: ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ strictly monotone with a 0 ≥ 1 (hence all terms positive) such that for every rational t not equal to any −a_n, the real series Σ 1/(a_n + t) has a rational sum (HasSum, so genuine convergence rather than tsum's junk value). Faithful.
